old: Demonstrates seed reproducibility — an 8x8 grid of colored cubes generated from a seed. Same seed always produces the same pattern. Slider changes seed, Replay regenerates identically, Random picks a new seed.
new: Two seeded colour grids can replay the same draw procedure or compare it with one discarded draw before RGB assignment. The same seed is not sufficient when the procedure changes. A slider selects an integer seed; REPLAY rebuilds, RANDOM chooses a seed, and optional draw strips expose the stream offset.

old: Wall-mounted Shannon entropy gauge — generates a random sequence, computes symbol frequencies, and displays H = -Σ p(x) log₂ p(x). Bar gauge fills from 0 to max entropy (~3.32 bits for 10 symbols). Frequency histogram shows symbol distribution.
new: Measures the empirical categorical Shannon entropy of a seeded sample from its symbol counts. The optional ledger retains the ordered tiles, compares a second weighted sample and sorts a display copy without changing counts or H. Disclosure reveals or withholds the measurement; it does not measure spatial disorder or thermodynamic entropy.

old: Shannon entropy as foundational axiom — information content measured by surprise. The mathematical bedrock of information theory: uncertainty is quantifiable.
new: A field of points whose random displacement grows along the grid’s z direction. It contrasts lattice alignment with positional variation; this artifact does not calculate Shannon entropy.

old: Extrudes the classic 10 PRINT pattern into a standing maze and animates an ant pathfinder through it.
new: A standing field of binary diagonal marks, with a separate ant search on a finer raster. The shipped stroke scene changes one diagonal every 0.08 seconds; its stored orientation and navigation update together. A visual contour is not a guarantee of a bodily passage. Character, wall and tile impressions are additional representations; the tile variant needs a separate orientation review.

old: A VR dice on a felt table. Grab and throw the dice — roll a 6 and 100 balls rain from the sky, roll a 1 and just 1 ball falls. Tracks roll statistics showing convergence to discrete uniform distribution with expected value 3.5.
new: A physical simulated die on a felt table, with face frequencies and a running mean read from settled orientation. Equal face probabilities and mean 3.5 are comparison hypotheses, not guarantees about a user’s throwing procedure. Rewards default to 16 balls per pip: 96 for a six and 16 for a one.

old: Five random walkers in a reflecting glass tank: fixed-length 2D/3D proposals or bounded power-law LEVY steps. The default tail keeps 200 previous positions; the optional logbook stand exposes the named seed, two clocks and ONE/ALL visual emphasis.
new: Five random walkers in a reflecting glass tank: fixed-length 2D/3D proposals or bounded inverse-square-root LONG STEP proposals. The legacy LEVY_FLIGHT enum remains compatible. A 200-position tail and optional logbook expose the named seed, two clocks and ONE/ALL emphasis.

old: Two standing 2D decay stacks rendered with MultiMesh: 1m cubes and 1dm prisms that gradually drift, rotate, sink, and darken.
new: Two MultiMesh stacks accumulate bounded drift, rotation, sinking and darkening at different configured rates. Both use fixed one-metre specimen units by default. Optional stack_fit fits both complete displays to a given width with a common geometry scale, a 0.6m gap and floor-aligned initial faces; controls retain full size. TOGGLE preserves the ramp clock; RESET restarts it.

old: Seeded sampling of six places and independently sampled silhouette dress. Bounded non-hostile arrivals with replay.
new: Seeded sampling without replacement fills six authored places. DRESS resamples the wardrobe; FORMS switches branching instructions while retaining its dress seed. Both leave arrival order unchanged; REPLAY restores that order. Flat billboard figures gain different outlines, not locomotion.

old: Side-by-side 16x16 heightfield grids comparing white noise (chaotic) and Perlin noise (terrain-like). Shows how gradient noise transforms raw randomness into coherent structure through spatial memory.
new: Compare seeded uniform heights with FastNoiseLite Perlin samples in two 16×16 grids. Frequency changes the scale of spatial correlation. Both fields use comparable column displays, while their sampling procedures and distributions differ.

old: Fractal Brownian Motion noise mixer — layers multiple sin-based noise octaves with controllable lacunarity and persistence. 128x128 floor texture with earth-tone color ramp. VR sliders adjust octaves (1–8), lacunarity (1.5–3.0), and persistence (0.3–0.7) to explore how complexity emerges from layered simple functions.
new: A visual mixer of finite sine-based spatial layers with seeded offsets. OCT, LAC and PER regenerate the sum live; each texture is normalized to its own range before an earth-toned palette is applied.

old: Throw darts at a square with an inscribed circle. The ratio of inside/outside hits converges to pi/4. Live counter shows estimate of pi improving with each dart. Green dots inside circle, red dots outside.
new: Uniform generated points estimate an inscribed circle’s area fraction; four times inside/total estimates pi. THROW, AUTO and RESET expose finite sampling, whose estimate need not improve with every point.

old: A cycling study of 100 particles: random kicks with memory, smooth trigonometric flow, spiral patterns, swarming and selection. These are distinct update rules, not five strengths of one noise source.
new: Five cycling particle studies: persistent random pushes, smooth trigonometric flow, spiral patterns, flocking-style interactions and target-ranked following. The selection chapter moves a fixed set of particles; it does not breed a population.

old: Swarm-based terrain generation where agents deposit pheromone trails that shape the landscape. Demonstrates emergent self-organization from simple local rules.
new: Walkers deposit decaying pheromone and accumulate visual height. Existing trail, sniff, avoid and grid rules change which local signal is followed. An optional paused comparison exposes attraction and avoidance from the same seed and starting walkers, with single-step, 20-step and replay controls.
